root_cause.text: The u32 classifier in net/sched/cls_u32.c computes an offset (`toff`, `off + n->sel.hoff`, etc.) from packet data or user control without ensuring it is non-negative, and passes it to `skb_header_pointer()`, which fails to validate negative offsets, leading to slab-out-of-bounds reads.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "skb_header_pointer() does not fully validate negative @offset values", and the patch replaces calls to `skb_header_pointer()` with `skb_header_pointer_careful()`, which properly handles negative offsets. The removed check `if (skb_headroom(skb) + toff > INT_MAX)` only guarded against large positive offsets, not negative ones, allowing a crafted negative offset to bypass validation and trigger the KASAN slab-out-of-bounds reported at `u32_classify+0x1180` (line 221 in cls_u32.c).
